item.title: Vital Water Desalination Plants in Iran and Bahrain are Attacked
item.summary: Strikes on non-military infrastructure are a “serious escalation,” analysts say, and could widen the war’s impact on civilians.

item.title: A Loose Band of Emerging Powers Is Divided Over Iran
item.summary: Brazil, China and Russia all denounced the U.S.-Israeli attacks, but other nations in the BRICS group haven’t, even though Iran is a fellow member.

item.title: Iran Could Retrieve Uranium at Site U.S. Bombed Last Year, Officials Say
item.summary: The fate of the highly enriched uranium and the options for securing it have become critical issues for the Trump administration.

item.title: Israel Strikes Oil Facilities in Iran
item.summary: Huge flames erupted into the sky over Tehran and a nearby city on Saturday.

item.title: Iran’s De Facto Leader Says Iran Will Not Surrender or Stop Its Attacks
item.summary: Ali Larijani, the head of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council and a close confidant of Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, said Iran was determined to avenge the killing of the leader.

item.title: In War’s First Week, a Punishing Military Campaign With No Coherent Endgame
item.summary: The U.S. and Israel have pounded Iran’s leadership and undercut its defense capabilities, but President Trump has offered wildly different explanations for what he hopes to achieve.

item.title: Deadly Clashes in Lebanon as Israel Renews Search for Missing Airman
item.summary: Dozens were killed in the Bekaa Valley overnight, the Lebanese health authorities said, amid airstrikes and intense violence in the town of Nabi Sheet.

item.title: Iranian President’s Apology to Neighboring Gulf States Showcases Leadership Rifts
item.summary: Masoud Pezeshkian, the Iranian president, apologized for Iranian strikes on Gulf states before backtracking after criticism from other Iranian leaders. Despite his remarks, Iran has continued its attacks.

item.title: Recent U.S. Assessment Found an Attack on Iran Unlikely to Result in Regime Change
item.summary: Intelligence officials have been skeptical that a popular uprising could dislodge the Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps, which controls much of Iran’s security apparatus.

item.title: Europe Didn’t Want War With Iran. But So Far, It Can’t Stay Out of It.
item.summary: From London to Rome and beyond, leaders are facing diplomatic headwinds and criticism at home as they take part in a conflict they did not seek.
